The viewport itself manages a stable reserve element that provides the missing scroll range while the assistant response grows.

## Core Concepts

### Viewport & Auto-Scroll

`Viewport` is the scrollable container. It auto-scrolls to the bottom as new content streams in, but only if the user hasn't scrolled up manually. Expanding a disclosure inside a message, such as a collapsible tool call card (a control with `aria-expanded="false"` that opens no popup, or the `<summary>` of a closed `<details>`), pauses it so the card stays where the user opened it; other clicks, text selection and keystrokes keep following, and scrolling back to the bottom or using `ThreadPrimitive.ScrollToBottom` resumes it. A new run or a thread switch also ends the pause. Set `autoScroll={false}` to disable this entirely.
    
    `<ThreadPrimitive.Viewport autoScroll={true}>
      {/* messages */}
    </ThreadPrimitive.Viewport>`

### Turn Anchor

By default, new messages appear at the bottom and scroll down. With `turnAnchor="top"`, the user's message anchors to the top of the viewport. The question stays at the top and the response streams in below it.
    
    `<ThreadPrimitive.Viewport turnAnchor="top">
      {/* messages */}
    </ThreadPrimitive.Viewport>`

When `turnAnchor="top"` is set, `MessagePrimitive.Root` registers the latest assistant message as the top-anchor target and the preceding user message as the anchor, so no additional component is required. The viewport itself manages a stable reserve element that provides the missing scroll range while the assistant response grows. This is the behavior used by the Thread component by default.

Use `topAnchorMessageClamp` to control how much of a long user message remains visible when `turnAnchor="top"`. Messages up to `tallerThan` stay fully visible. For messages taller than that, `visibleHeight` controls how much of the message's bottom edge remains visible above the assistant response:
    
    `<ThreadPrimitive.Viewport
      turnAnchor="top"
      topAnchorMessageClamp={{ tallerThan: "10em", visibleHeight: "6em" }}
    >
      {/* messages */}
    </ThreadPrimitive.Viewport>`

### Viewport Scroll Options

`ThreadPrimitive.Viewport` has three event-specific scroll controls:

  * `scrollToBottomOnRunStart` (default `true`): scrolls when `thread.runStart` fires; it has no effect with `turnAnchor="top"`
  * `scrollToBottomOnInitialize` (default `true`): scrolls when the thread's messages first load
  * `scrollToBottomOnThreadSwitch` (default `true`): scrolls when `threads.selectionChanged` fires

These work alongside `autoScroll`. If `autoScroll` is omitted, it defaults to `true` for `turnAnchor="bottom"` and `false` for `turnAnchor="top"`.
    
    `<ThreadPrimitive.Viewport
      turnAnchor="top"
      autoScroll={false}
      scrollToBottomOnRunStart={true}
      scrollToBottomOnInitialize={false}
      scrollToBottomOnThreadSwitch={true}
    >
      <ThreadPrimitive.Messages>
        {({ message }) => {
          if (message.role === "user") return <UserMessage />;
          return <AssistantMessage />;
        }}
      </ThreadPrimitive.Messages>
    </ThreadPrimitive.Viewport>`

### ViewportFooter

### Row

Renders one row of a thread flattened by `createThreadRowsSelector`, for virtualized lists: a whole user or system message (or any message being edited), one top-level node of an assistant message's part grouping, or the end of a turn. It mounts only the row's message scope and, for a part row, only that row's parts; a row whose message has left the thread renders nothing. The render function switches on `type`, and a part row receives `part` and `children` exactly as `MessagePrimitive.GroupedParts` passes them. See the virtualization guide.
    
    `const selectRows = createThreadRowsSelector();
    
    function Rows() {
      const rows = useAuiState(selectRows);
      return rows.map((row) => (
        <ThreadPrimitive.Row key={row.key} row={row}>
          {renderRow}
        </ThreadPrimitive.Row>
      ));
    }`

### ScrollToBottom

Scrolls the viewport to the bottom. Disabled when the viewport is already at the bottom. Renders a `<button>` element unless `asChild` is set.
    
    `<ThreadPrimitive.ScrollToBottom className="rounded-full bg-background p-2 shadow-md">
      <ArrowDownIcon />
    </ThreadPrimitive.ScrollToBottom>`

Prop

Type

`behavior?`
    
    `ScrollBehavior`

### LoadEarlier

Loads the page before the first loaded message through `aui.thread.loadEarlier()`. Disabled while `thread.hasEarlier` is false; a press while a page loads (`thread.isLoadingEarlier`) joins that load, so the button keeps keyboard focus until the page lands. The runtime decides both, for example an external store adapter's `hasEarlier` and `onLoadEarlier`. Renders a `<button>` element unless `asChild` is set. The viewport keeps the visible messages in place when the page lands above them.
    
    `<AuiIf condition={(s) => s.thread.hasEarlier || s.thread.isLoadingEarlier}>
      <ThreadPrimitive.LoadEarlier className="self-center text-sm">
        Load earlier messages
      </ThreadPrimitive.LoadEarlier>
    </AuiIf>`

### Viewport

A scrollable viewport container for thread messages. This component provides a scrollable area for displaying thread messages with automatic scrolling capabilities. It manages the viewport state and provides context for child components to access viewport-related functionality.

This primitive renders a `<div>` element unless `asChild` is set.
    
    `<ThreadPrimitive.Viewport turnAnchor="top">
      <ThreadPrimitive.Messages>
